title: AI Guard policies: detector settings, policy control rules, first-match order, applications and testing

prose.text: An AI Guard policy is a set of detector settings; it applies to traffic only through a policy control rule that matches it. Both halves are covered here.

prose.label: Policy configurations.

checks.do: The rules above the expected one in policy control order, since evaluation stops at the first match.

That the rule is enabled and its criteria match the traffic: provider and model, account type, users or groups for user rules; applications, credentials, application groups, source IPs or custom headers for application rules.

The detector's Action (Block, Detect or Allow) and threshold in the policy; Detect only flags. Which direction counts as strict for the threshold is disputed, so state the direction by what triggers rather than by strict.
Run the policy through Policy Testing with the same provider credential and model before relying on it.

policy-is-detectors.statement: A policy is set by enabling detectors on prompts and responses; a tenant can have several policies, apply one per app, several to one app, or one to several apps.

quotes: You set a policy by enabling one or more included detectors on prompts and responses.
Every policy is a guardrail, and you can set up multiple policies, define and apply a policy per app, apply multiple policies to one app, or apply a policy to multiple apps.

detector-settings.statement: Most prompt detectors share Enabled (on by default), Severity, Threshold (the page words it as: the lower the threshold setting, the more strict AI Guard is with activating the policy) and Action: Allow lets the prompt proceed, Block blocks it, Detect flags it as detected, and some detectors also offer Disabled.

quotes: Most prompt detectors share the following configuration options:
Enabled: Enables the prompt detector and is on by default.
Severity: Corresponds to the severity icons in the Prompt Detectors column on the Policies page.
Threshold: The lower the threshold setting, the more strict AI Guard is with activating the policy (i.e., allowing, blocking, or detecting the prompt).
Allow allows the prompt to proceed, Block blocks the prompt, and Detect flags the prompt as detected.
Some detectors include a Disabled option to ensure what is disabled is not covered under that category's detections.

pii-name-disabled.statement: In the PII detector the Person's name category defaults to Disabled.

quotes: In the PII detector, the Person's name category is defaulted to Disabled.

ten-limit.statement: Competition and Topic accept at most 10 entries at a time in a single policy, and the Topic/Off Topic runbook gives the Off Topic topic definitions up to 10 topics as well.

quotes: Only 10 can be set at a time for a single policy.
evidence.after: Competition: Includes a Competitors category where you enter your specific competitor names.

quotes: Only 10 can be set at a time for a single policy.
evidence.after: Topic: Includes the ability to add multiple custom topics to add to your policy.

quotes: Custom Topic (Topic) or Topic Definition (Off Topic): Up to 10 topics. Each has a Name and a Definition.

control-binding.statement: A policy configuration is applied by attaching it through policy control to an LLM provider, user or user group; policy controls are evaluated top to bottom and evaluation stops at the first match.

quotes: After you create an AI Guard policy configuration, you can then attach it to an LLM provider, user, or user group by adding policy control.
Policies are evaluated from top-to-bottom and the evaluation will stop after matching the first policy.

user-control-fields.statement: A user policy control needs a rule name, a policy configuration, a rule order and a rule status (enabled or disabled), and at least one match criterion among LLM provider and models (with Account Type when Organization Restrictions are on), users and user groups.

quotes: Rule Name: Enter a name for the policy match.
Policy Configuration: From the drop-down menu, select a policy you previously created.
Rule Order: Enter a number for the order in which you want the policy match applied.
Rule Status: Select whether you want the rule to be enabled or disabled.
Match Criteria: At least one match criteria must be defined:
Account Type: If Organization Restrictions are enabled, select Enterprise, Personal, or Both.
Users: Click the drop-down menu and select the users you want to include with the match criteria.
User Groups: Click the drop-down to select the groups you want to include in the match criteria.

criteria-types.statement: In the API a match rule's criteria have one of three types: `APPLICATION` targets LLM applications (optionally specific application credentials), application groups, LLM providers, source IPs and optional custom request headers; `DAS_APPLICATION` targets DAS applications the same way without providers; `USER` targets Zscaler users and user groups, optionally narrowed by LLM provider.

expect.description: Polymorphic base for match-rule criteria; the `type` discriminator selects the concrete subtype (APPLICATION, USER, or DAS_APPLICATION).
Match criteria targeting LLM applications, application groups, LLM providers, source IPs, and optional custom request headers.
Selects a specific LLM application (by id or name) and, optionally, particular application credentials.
Match criteria targeting DAS applications, identified by LLM applications, application groups, source IPs, and optional custom request headers.
Match criteria targeting specific Zscaler users and user groups, optionally narrowed by LLM provider.

match-rule-references.statement: Creating a match rule through the API requires the detection policy and any LLM applications it names to exist already; otherwise the request is rejected with a message naming the missing item.

expect.description:
Creates a new detection policy match rule with priority ordering. The detection policy and any
LLM applications the rule refers to must already exist; if a referenced policy or application
cannot be found, the request is rejected with a message that names the missing item.

no-match-unapplied.statement: A policy configuration applies to traffic only through an enabled policy control that matches it first; a policy with no such rule, a disabled rule, or a rule below an earlier match is not applied to that traffic.
no-match-unapplied.conditions: Follows from first-match evaluation and the rule status field; no page describes the failure case.

enable-disable-match-rules.statement: Enabling or disabling a detection policy through the API turns every match rule that references it on or off, and the response lists those rules with their new state; disabling does not delete the policy.

expect.description: Result of enabling or disabling a detection policy. Enabling or disabling a policy turns every match rule that references it on or off; the response lists those match rules with their new state rather than the full policy.
Disables the detection policy without deleting it.

ai-applications.statement: AI applications such as chatbots are added while configuring AI Guard so a policy can be applied to them; they can be grouped into application groups; in DAS/API mode an application carries API keys, and in Proxy mode an identity broker.

quotes: Adding an AI application (such as a chatbot) needs to be done while configuring AI Guard. Once added, an AI Guard policy can be configured and applied to it.
Applications: From the drop-down menu, select the applications you want to group together.
To make changes to a Proxy mode AI application's identity broker:

testing.statement: Policy Testing, available once an LLM provider, its credentials and a policy exist, sends a prompt through a chosen provider credential, policy and LLM model and shows what was allowed or blocked together with the prompt and response without guardrails.

quotes: After adding a large language model (LLM) provider, LLM provider credentials, and a policy to AI Guard, you can test your policy to make sure it is working to your satisfaction.
Provider Credential: From the drop-down menu, select an LLM credential.
Policy: From the drop-down menu, select a policy you want to test.
LLM Model: From the drop-down menu, select the LLM model you want to use.
In addition to the policy test showing you what is allowed or blocked, it also shows you the prompt and response without guardrails.

quickstart-example-policy.statement: The ChatGPT and Microsoft 365 Copilot quick starts' example policy configuration enables the Toxicity prompt detector and skips response detectors, then, if everything looks correct, clicks Submit Policy; the Review tab shows a summary of the policy configuration.

quotes: On the Prompt Detectors tab, click on the Toxicity detector and then click on Save Changes.
Skip the configuration of response detectors.
The Review tab shows you a summary of the policy configuration you created.
Click Submit Policy if everything looks correct.

config-view-details.statement: A policy configuration's View Details button under Action opens the View Configuration Details window, which shows, among other things, its description, controls, prompt detectors and response detectors.

quotes: To view details of a policy configuration, under Action, click the View Details button. The View Configuration Details window appears and shows you the following information:
- Description
- Controls
- Prompt Detectors
- Response Detectors

config-edit-copy-delete.statement: A policy configuration can be edited or copied from the Action column, each opening an Edit Policy or Copy Configuration page; deleting one requires typing Delete into a text field and then clicking Delete.

quotes: Under the Action column, click the Edit Configuration icon. The Edit Policy page opens.
Under the Action column, click the Copy Configuration icon. The Copy Configuration page opens.
Type Delete into the text field to confirm the deletion of the policy, and then click the Delete button.

app-control-criteria.statement: On the AI Guard for Apps page, a policy configuration is attached to an application by adding policy control, on the AI Applications tab in Proxy mode (for DAS mode the page says to skip to the next step); the rule takes a rule name, a policy configuration, a rule order and a rule status (enabled or disabled), and at least one match criterion defined among LLM Provider & Models (Proxy Only), Applications & Credentials, Application Groups, Custom Request Headers and their values, and source IPv4 addresses; the new policy control appears at the Rule Order number entered.

quotes: After you create an AI Guard policy configuration, you can then attach it to an application by adding policy control.
Click the AI Applications tab in Proxy mode. For DAS mode, skip to the next step.
Rule Name: Enter a name for the policy match.
Policy Configuration: From the drop-down menu, select a policy you previously created.
Rule Order: Enter a number for the order in which you want the policy match applied.
Rule Status: Select whether you want the rule to be enabled or disabled.
Match Criteria: At least one match criteria must be defined:
LLM Provider & Models (Proxy Only): Match against specific LLM providers and models.
Applications & Credentials: Match against specific AI Applications and their credentials.
Application Groups: Match against specific AI Application Groups.
Custom Request Headers: Match against custom request headers and their values.
Source IPs: Match against specific source IPv4 addresses (e.g., 192.168.1.1).
The new policy control appears at the Rule Order number you entered.

allowlist.statement: The prompt allowlist holds prompts to allow that may otherwise be blocked by an existing AI Guard policy; it is available only in Proxy mode, and prompts sent to the allowlist endpoint are fully encrypted so the prompt content remains protected end to end.

quotes: The prompt allowlist for AI Guard allows you to track and manage any prompts that you wish to allow that may otherwise be blocked by an existing AI Guard policy.
Prompts sent to the allowlist endpoint are fully encrypted, so the prompt content remains protected end-to-end.
The prompt allowlist functionality is only available in Proxy mode.
The prompt allowlist for AI Guard allows you to track and manage any prompts that you wish to allow that may otherwise be blocked by an existing AI Guard policy.
Prompts sent to the allowlist endpoint are fully encrypted, so the prompt content remains protected end-to-end.
The prompt allowlist functionality is only available in Proxy mode.

allowlist-prereqs.statement: Using the allowlist requires Store Prompts/Responses and Enable Data Sharing for AI Training enabled under Security Settings and the System Administrator role with all-write access; individual actions are governed by the Default Access permission: View to see allowlisted prompts, Create to add to the allowlist and Delete to delete a prompt from it.

quotes: Under Security Settings, enable Store Prompts/Responses and Enable Data Sharing for AI Training.
Using the allowlist functionality requires the System Administrator role with all-write access. Individual actions are governed by the Default Access permission.
View allowlisted prompts: Default Access: View
Add to allowlist: Default Access: Create
Delete prompt from allowlist: Default Access: Delete

allowlist-add.statement: A blocked prompt is added to the allowlist from the Transaction Details window: under Prompt Details, Reveal Prompt, then Add to Allowlist if the blocked prompt is the one to add; added prompts are found on the Prompt Allowlist page, where a prompt is deleted with Delete in the Action column.

quotes: At the bottom of the Transaction Details window under Prompt Details, click Reveal Prompt.
If the blocked prompt is the one you want to add to the allowlist, click Add to Allowlist.
On the Prompt Allowlist page, you can find the prompts that you have added.
On the Prompt Allowlist page, find the prompt you want to delete and in the Action column, click Delete.

no-detector-allowlist.statement: The Competition runbook says allowlisting is not supported at the Competition-detector level, and the Topic/Off Topic runbook says it is not supported at the detector level; both point to policy-level exceptions (exclude a user group, restrict to certain apps), and the Competition runbook adds a sentence-level allow rule if you have those.

quotes: Not supported at the Competition-detector level. Use policy-level exceptions (exclude a user group, restrict to certain apps) or a sentence-level allow rule if you have those.
Not supported at the detector level. Use policy-level exceptions (exclude a user group, restrict to certain apps).

threshold-scale.statement: The PII runbook defines the threshold as a number between 0.0 and 1.0 that controls how confident the model must be before it calls a prompt a match, comparing it to a volume knob: turned up, only very obvious mentions trigger; turned down, more borderline cases trigger too.

quotes: The threshold is a number between 0.0 and 1.0 that controls how confident the model must be before it calls a prompt a match.
Think of it as a volume knob: turn it up and only very obvious mentions trigger. Turn it down and more borderline cases trigger too.

runbook-rollout.statement: Each of the PII, IP, Competition and Topic/Off Topic runbooks gives Severity as LOW for initial deployments, raised to MEDIUM or HIGH only after a user confirms the false-positive rate is acceptable, and says to validate in Policy Testing with five to ten sample prompts; each describes the detector's default on triggering as Detect (log only), Allow (pass through) or Block (stop the prompt), labeled Default State in the PII, Competition and Topic/Off Topic runbooks and Action in the IP runbook; the PII runbook adds that after creating a policy and confirming it works the next step is to create a policy match.

quotes: Severity: Corresponds to the severity icons in the Prompt Detectors column on the Policies page. The recommended setting is LOW for initial deployments. Raise to MEDIUM/HIGH only after a user confirms the false-positive rate is acceptable.
Validate in Policy Testing with five to ten sample prompts to confirm your setup is working as expected.

strict-direction.summary: Which direction of the detector threshold is strict: the policy page says a lower threshold is more strict, the PII runbook calls the high end stricter.

positions.says: The policy configuration page says the lower the threshold setting, the more strict AI Guard is with activating the policy (allowing, blocking or detecting the prompt).

quotes: Threshold: The lower the threshold setting, the more strict AI Guard is with activating the policy (i.e., allowing, blocking, or detecting the prompt).

positions.says: The PII runbook labels the 0.7 to 1.00 range Stricter, where only high-confidence matches trigger, and describes turning the threshold up as meaning only very obvious mentions trigger.

quotes: | 0.7 to 1.00 | Stricter. Only high-confidence matches trigger. | If you are sensitive to noise from extended categories (PERSON, LOCATION, DATE/TIME). |
Think of it as a volume knob: turn it up and only very obvious mentions trigger. Turn it down and more borderline cases trigger too.

strict-direction.impact: On the mechanics the pages agree that a lower threshold makes more prompts trigger; they differ on whether strict means more enforcement (lower) or tighter matching (higher), so describe the direction by what triggers rather than by strict.

allowlist-scope.summary: Whether the allowlist covers responses as well as prompts: the allowlist page names only prompts, the detection summary says a blocked prompt or response can be added.

positions.says: The allowlist page describes it as an allowlist of prompts that an AI Guard policy may otherwise block, and its add and delete steps name only prompts.

quotes: The prompt allowlist for AI Guard allows you to track and manage any prompts that you wish to allow that may otherwise be blocked by an existing AI Guard policy.
If the blocked prompt is the one you want to add to the allowlist, click Add to Allowlist.

positions.says: The detection summary page says that with the proper permissions, revealing a blocked prompt or response offers Add to Allowlist for the prompt or response.

quotes: Add to Allowlist: If you have the proper permissions, when you reveal a prompt or response that was blocked, you can click this option to add the prompt or response to your allowlist.

allowlist-scope.impact: Whether a blocked response can be allowlisted is unsettled; answer for prompts and say the detection summary page also mentions responses.

config-delete-referenced.title: Is deleting a policy configuration that a policy control still references blocked, and what happens to those controls?
config-delete-referenced.detail: For the API, [[ai-security.ai-guard.admin-api:delete-409]] answers: a referenced delete returns 409. The portal page for managing policy configurations does not say whether deleting a configuration that a policy control still references is blocked, or what happens to those controls, so the portal behavior is open.

no-match-default.title: What AI Guard does with traffic that no policy control matches
no-match-default.detail: No captured page says whether unmatched traffic is allowed uninspected, inspected by a default policy, or blocked. The ZIA integration names AllUsersGroup as the default user group (ai-security.ai-guard.zia-integration:users-appear), which does not say what policy applies to it.
no-match-default.blocks: answers on traffic outside every policy control
